cases.label: lazy-iterator
cases.note: The engine returns a lazy sequence and the caller takes 5. The only behaviour that composes with a scheduler.

cases.label: caller-bounded
cases.note: The engine requires an explicit window and returns the same prefix.

cases.label: materialise
cases.note: Engines whose only API materialises the whole set hang or exhaust memory. Recorded as a result, not excused.

expectation.note: 'Repeats forever' is normative; what an API does with it is not.

normative_evidence.quote: If neither the COUNT nor UNTIL rule parts are present, the recurrence rule is considered to repeat forever.

rationale: RFC 5545 places no bound on expansion cost. Every practical engine must therefore add a policy the standard does not define, and the corpus records which one.
title: Infinite recurrence with no COUNT and no UNTIL
